why: Regions are task types and minGap is the cooldown between two runs of the same type: the task-scheduler problem. The most frequent region builds a skeleton of (maxFreq-1) blocks of width minGap+1, ties fill the last block, and the answer is never below n.
hints: Only the count per region matters. Which region dictates the idle time?
Place the most frequent region first with minGap slots between copies; other regions fill those gaps. The skeleton length is (maxFreq - 1) * (minGap + 1) + (number of regions tied at maxFreq).
Count with a 26-slot array, compute the skeleton, return max(n, skeleton). O(n).
pitfalls: When the other regions overflow the gaps, there is no idle time: return n, not the skeleton.
Count every region tied for the maximum frequency in the last block.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ n = requests.length ≤ 10^5
  • 0 ≤ minGap ≤ 100
  • requests contains lowercase English letters
